newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's urban unemployment rate on the rise.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's urban unemployment rate on the rise.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 16 Reuter - Nearly 13 percent of the workforce in Colombia's seven leading cities was unemployed in January through March, a 2.5 percent increase over the first quarter of 1996, the National Statistics Department DANE said Wednesday.
It said the rate of joblessness during the three-month period, officially tallied at 12.7 percent, was also up 1.4 percent over December 1996.

A total of 5.57 million people were employed in the country's leading metropolitan areas in December, compared to 5.47 million in March, the DANE said, adding that 100,000 workers had been dropped from payrolls during the three-month period.

The capital, Bogota, had the lowest rate of joblessness in the first quarter, at 9.4 percent, while Cali and Medellin were saddled with the highest rates at 17.4 percent and 16.4 percent respectively.
DANE offered no estimate of rural unemployment, but economic analysts say it is roughly double the urban rate.

The lack of job opportunities, coupled with a long-running crisis in the agricultural sector and mounting political violence, has forced tens of thousands of Colombians to migrate to metropolitan areas in recent years.

DANE gave no specific reasons for the increase in urban unemployment in its quarterly report. But its latest statistics come against the backdrop of a sharp slowdown in economic growth last year. A recession in Colombia's construction sector has been cited in the past as a leading cause for the especially high unemployment rate in Cali.
